title: Makroudh
description: Semolina diamonds around a spiced date paste, fried until they set and dropped straight into warm honey. Makes about thirty pieces and they keep for a week in a tin.
notes: Semolina dough has to rest before it can be rolled — the grains need time to drink. Skip the rest and it crumbles along every cut.

steps.text: Rub the olive oil into the coarse semolina with your fingertips until every grain is coated and the bowl smells nutty.
steps.tip: This is the only real technique in the recipe. Oil-coated grains give a short, sandy bite; under-rubbed ones go hard.

steps.text: Sprinkle in the salt, warm water, and orange blossom water and press the mixture together without kneading it.
steps.tip: Semolina has no gluten worth developing. Kneading only compacts it — gather it, do not work it.

steps.text: Cover the bowl and leave it alone while the semolina swells.
Work the pitted dates with the cinnamon, orange zest, and butter into a smooth, pliable paste.
Roll a third of the dough into a long rope, press a channel down its length with the side of your finger, and lay a rope of date paste into it.
Close the dough over the filling, flatten the log gently with your palm, and cut it on the diagonal into diamonds.
Fry the diamonds in the neutral oil at a moderate heat, turning once, until they are set and pale gold.
steps.tip: Too hot and the outside colours before the inside cooks; a makroudh should be dry-crumbed in the middle, never doughy.

steps.text: Warm the honey in a wide pan and drop each piece in straight from the fryer, turning it until it is glossy.
steps.tip: Hot pastry into warm honey is the whole trick. Either one cold and the honey sits on the surface instead of soaking in.

steps.text: Lift them onto a rack, scatter with the sesame seeds, and leave them to set before stacking.
